newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Spot forint easing spurs Hungary futures FX sales.
newsitem.headline: Spot forint easing spurs Hungary futures FX sales.

text.p: Total Hungarian currency futures turnover rose for the second consecutive day on Thursday as the spot forint weakened versus the currency basket against which it floats, traders said.
The Budapest Commodities Exchange (BCE) recorded moderate turnover of 5.0 billion forints ($28.5 million), while the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) registered 361 million forints.

"We are in (a) special period at the moment on the spot market with the forint 50 points weaker than the resistance level. Some dealers think it might be worth selling forward," said BSE dealer Robert Cselovszki, of West LB Investment.

The forint normally stays close to the resistance level of the 4.5-percent central bank intervention band as it floats on the spot market against a currency basket made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar.
But on Wednesday, it weakened to 50 fillers inside the band and maintained the gap on Thursday.
"We expect the forint to close the gap to around 25 points over the next week so, some investors think now's the time to sell," Cselovski said.
All but five million forints of total BSE trade was in March marks or dollars.
March marks grabbed 249 million forints of trade and March dollar trades topped 109 million.
March marks fell 30 fillers to 104.75 forints and December added 89 fillers to 112.94.
March dollars rose 1.66 to 176.94 forints while December gained 1.32 to 193.47 forints.
At the BCE, most large trades were spread among the yen, dollar, mark and Swiss franc. But the dollar was most popular, accounting for 12,472 of the 32,005 lots traded.
The yen posted the largest gains, with March up 3.30 forints to 146.70. March dollars followed in terms of gains with a rise of 1.55 forints to 176.90.
Trading opened in March 1998 marks at 119.30 forints.
-- Duncan Shiels, Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040 ($ = 175.5 Hungarian Forints)
